meta.price_basis: Cheapest tournament-legal English paper non-foil printing, USD; memorabilia printings excluded.

cheap_help.title: What counts as cheap draw and ramp
counts: Ramp at any mana value: mana rocks, mana creatures, rituals, cost reducers, land ramp spells, and lands that make extra mana (Cabal Coffers, Nykthos).
Card draw and card selection that cost 2 or less: draw spells, looting, scry and other filtering.
cheap_help.not: Not counted: fetch lands, basics, and draw or selection costing 3 or more.
cheap_help.why: Each one lowers the land count by 0.28, so about 4 of them replace a land: they help you hit land drops or stand in for one (Karsten).
cheap_help.targets: Suggested: about 10 ramp and 8 to 10 cheap draw or selection, about 19 in all, the median of the real decks we test against.

estimate_defaults.basis: median of 15 real decks in the Step 1 drift fixtures

tiers.label: Tier 1b

tiers.label: Tier 2

cycles.name: Any-colour lands
cycles.why: Always untapped, every colour, free.

cycles.name: Any-colour lands for certain spells
cycles.why: Always include them if your deck meets the condition: any colour, untapped, for the spells named (Ancient Ziggurat for creatures, Cavern of Souls for your tribe). Skip them if few of your spells qualify.

cycles.name: Original duals (splurge)
cycles.why: Always untapped, no cost; typed, so fetch lands find them.

cycles.name: Shock lands
cycles.why: Untapped for 2 life; typed, so fetch lands find them.

cycles.name: Battlebond lands
cycles.why: Always untapped at a Commander table, no cost; not fetchable.

cycles.name: Gathering Place cycle
cycles.why: Always untapped; colour the turn you play it and on any later turn you control a basic, which is nearly always in a deck with basics. (Deckwright models it as tier 2; B-13.)

cycles.name: Pathways
cycles.why: Always untapped, no cost; each copy gives one colour once played.

cycles.name: Fetch lands
cycles.why: As fast as what they find; they earn their place fixing three-plus colours and add little in two.

cycles.name: Other always-untapped lands
cycles.why: Untapped with a small catch.

cycles.name: Verges
cycles.why: Always untapped; one colour always, the second once you control the matching basic type. (Deckwright models them as tier 2; B-13.)

cycles.name: Horizon lands
cycles.why: Always untapped; 1 life per coloured mana, and they cash in for a card.

cycles.name: Pain lands
cycles.why: Always untapped; colourless is free, colour costs 1 damage.

cycles.name: Filter lands
cycles.why: Always untapped; need another mana to turn into colours.

cycles.name: Any-colour lands with a cost
cycles.why: Always untapped, any colour for life or damage: strong in three-plus colours, worse than a dual in two. Starting Town is untapped only on turns 1-3.

cycles.name: Any-colour filters (pay 1)
cycles.why: Always untapped; pay 1 for any colour, so they fix without adding mana. Deckwright plays them only in three-plus colours.

cycles.name: Tainted lands and Nimbus Maze
cycles.why: Always untapped, but colourless unless you control the named basic; good only in decks heavy in it.

cycles.name: Reveal lands
cycles.why: Untapped if you reveal a matching card: 79-90% on turns 1-4 in Deckwright's model (tapped cost 0.15), the best conditional kind.

cycles.name: Fast lands
cycles.why: Untapped on turns 1-3, tapped later (tapped cost 0.25).

cycles.name: Check lands
cycles.why: Untapped once you control a matching basic type: 0% turn 1, 65% turn 2, 88% turn 3 (tapped cost 0.38).

cycles.name: Slow lands
cycles.why: Tapped on turns 1-2, untapped from turn 3 (tapped cost 0.50).

cycles.name: Turbulent lands
cycles.why: Untapped once your opponents control eight or more lands between them: about turn 3 at a four-player table, a little behind slow lands.

cycles.name: Battle lands
cycles.why: Untapped only with two basics out: 0% on turns 1-2, 29% on turn 3 (tapped cost 0.78), the weakest conditional kind.

cycles.name: Other conditional lands
cycles.why: Untapped always, but one of the colours only on a turn you played a land.

cycles.name: Tribal reveal lands
cycles.why: Untapped if you reveal a card of the named tribe: as good as a reveal land in that tribal deck, tapped in any other.

cycles.name: Planeswalker lands
cycles.why: Untapped only while you control a planeswalker: for planeswalker decks, tapped in nearly every other.

cycles.name: Low-life lands
cycles.why: Untapped once any player is at 13 life or less: tapped on the early turns that matter, untapped late.

cycles.name: Triomes
cycles.why: Never untapped. Three-plus colour decks still use them for fixing: three colours, cycling, fetchable.

cycles.name: Surveil lands
cycles.why: Never untapped; surveil 1, and two basic land types, so fetch lands find them. Three-plus colours, after the Triomes.

cycles.name: Cycling lands
cycles.why: Never untapped; cycling 2, and two basic land types, so fetch lands find them. Three-plus colours.

cycles.name: Snow duals
cycles.why: Never untapped; two basic land types, so fetch lands find them, and snow. Three-plus colours.

cycles.name: Tri-lands
cycles.why: Never untapped; three colours from one land, not fetchable. Three-plus colours on a budget.

cycles.name: Basic-fetch lands
cycles.why: Tapped or slow: trade themselves for a basic of any colour you need. Three-plus colours on a budget.

cycles.name: Thriving lands
cycles.why: Never untapped; one colour plus one you choose. Three-plus colours on a budget.

cycles.name: Temples (scry lands)
cycles.why: Never untapped; scry 1. Three-plus colours on a budget.

cycles.name: Gain lands
cycles.why: Never untapped; gain 1 life. Three-plus colours on a budget.

cycles.name: Tapped any-colour lands
cycles.why: Enter tapped but make any colour (Path of Ancestry: any in your commander's colours). Three-plus colours on a budget.

cycles.name: Bounce lands
cycles.why: Never untapped, and return a land: two mana from one land later. Three-plus colours, with care.

cycles.name: Fast mana (Game Changers, splurge)
cycles.why: The strongest rocks; bracket 4 only, and Grim Monolith wants an untap effect.

cycles.name: Core rocks
cycles.why: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone and Thran Dynamo: the research's fixed core. Mind Stone is now under Utility.

cycles.name: Talismans
cycles.why: Core pair rock: 2 mana, untapped, both colours; 1 damage for colour.

cycles.name: Signets
cycles.why: Core pair rock: 2 mana, both colours at once; needs 1 to start.

cycles.name: Medallions
cycles.why: Cost reducers: first rock after the core in a mono-colour deck; in two colours, ahead of any 3-mana rock but behind the 2-mana rocks (R17-F7, F15).

cycles.name: Mono-colour rocks
cycles.why: Rocks of one colour: plain ones are rare (The Soul Stone, The Mind Stone); the rest restrict what the mana casts, which suits the right deck (R17-F4).

cycles.name: Lockets
cycles.why: Pair rock at 3 mana: the best 3-mana rock in two colours, added after the Talisman and Signet, never instead of them; cash in for two cards (R17-F16).

cycles.name: Budget and three-colour rocks
cycles.why: Honest picks behind the cycles above: 2-mana rocks that enter tapped (one colour you choose), a basic onto the battlefield, or three colours from one 3-mana rock for a three-colour deck on a budget.

cycles.name: Combo and conditional rocks
cycles.why: Strong only when a condition holds (legends, three artifacts, creatures to tap or sacrifice, devotion, a creature type) or as a combo piece; excellent in the right deck, dead in others.

cycles.name: Big rocks (4+)
cycles.why: 4 mana or more for two or more mana a turn: late ramp into big spells, after the 2- and 3-mana rocks; ahead of Mono-colour payoffs only outside mono-colour decks.

cycles.name: Mono-colour payoffs
cycles.why: Big rocks that pay off a deck of one colour. My additions; Deckwright's research does not cover them.

cycles.name: Utility rocks
cycles.why: Rocks chosen for their extra effect (R17-F2, F14, F17).

cycles.name: Utility lands
cycles.why: My picks: Deckwright flags utility lands but does not rank them yet (B-15).

cycles.name: Basic upgrades
cycles.why: One-colour lands that replace a basic and add an effect.

steps.done: This step is done when your colours are set (paste a deck, pick a commander or pick colours).
steps.title: Your deck
explain: Paste your decklist, or start from a commander, to get your land count and the colour sources you need. Or just pick your colours. The steps that follow show only the cards for those colours.
Lands: 31.42 + 3.13 × average mana value − 0.28 × cheap draw and ramp spells (Karsten's 99-card formula); most decks land at 35 to 38.
Colour sources: about 19 for a colour you need early, 28 to 30 for a double pip like WW or 1GG, 33 to 36 for a triple; a gold card needs one more of each.
Plan 6 to 10 of the lands as utility lands, inside the count, not on top of it. About 10 ramp pieces is typical.

steps.done: This step is done when you’ve added the free ones and any your deck qualifies for.
steps.title: Any-colour lands

steps.done: This step is done when your colour sources are close to the targets from Step 1, or your budget runs out.
steps.empty: Single-colour decks skip this step: every land you need is in Steps 2, 4 and 5.
steps.title: Lands that make two or more of your colours
explain: An untapped land can be used the turn you play it; a tapped one makes you wait a turn, so untapped lands come first. Take from the top until your coloured lands are filled. Tier 1 is always untapped, 1b untapped with a cost, 2 untapped once a condition is met, 3 never untapped; aim for as close to zero tapped lands as your budget allows. In three or more colours, tapped duals with fixing value come last (Triomes first, then surveil, cycling and snow duals, then budget tapped duals), taken only while a colour is still short.

groups.title: Lands that make two or more of your colours

steps.done: This step is done when you have 6 to 10 utility lands, counting the ones from earlier steps.
steps.title: Utility lands
explain: First the ones that make your colours: each replaces a basic and costs nothing in colour. Then colourless ones by job: each takes a coloured source's slot. Stay inside the utility budget from Step 1.

In one or two colours, the research staples come first: Craft it for me adds them to open slots while your colours stay covered. In three or more colours, every slot is needed for colour. The rest are yours to pick by job.

groups.title: Utility lands that make your colours
groups.intro: Each replaces a basic of its colour. Most reliably untapped first; inside a group, my read of the effect.

groups.title: Colourless staples from research
groups.intro: Universal picks for one and two colours: worth a colourless slot in almost any deck. Take them while every colour still meets its source count.

groups.title: Colourless utility lands
groups.intro: Each takes a coloured source's slot. Pick by job.

steps.done: This step is done when your land count matches Step 1.
steps.title: Basics
explain: Fill the rest of the land count with basics in proportion to your colour pips.
Keep enough of them for the lands that count basics: check lands, battle lands, Castles, Gathering Place and the any-basic lands.

steps.done: This step is done when your rocks plus your deck’s other ramp come to about 10.
steps.title: Rocks
explain: Take the core, then your identity's rocks (the pair's Talisman and Signet, a Medallion in one or two colours). Then add utility rocks for what your deck needs. Deckwright's architecture sets the ramp count; about 10 is typical.

groups.title: Every deck
groups.intro: The core rocks, then the Game Changer fast mana (bracket 4 only).
